chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Mūsā, from Zurārah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a man who goes out on a journey intending it, then the time enters for him while he has gone out from the village by two farsakhs, so they prayed and departed. Then one of them turned aside for some need, and it was not decreed for him to continue the departure. What should he do regarding the prayer that he had prayed as two rakʿahs? He عليه السلام said: His prayer is complete, and he does not repeat.

Thus, the correct way of understanding this report is one of two things: one of them is that if the time had passed, repetition was not required of him; rather, repetition is only binding upon him so long as the time remains. The second is that even if it was not decreed for him to continue the departure, he had not turned back from the intention of travel, and whenever that is so, repetition is not required of him; rather, shortening remains binding upon him up to thirty days, as we have explained in the major book.

key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: repetition of the prayer within its time
key_terms.الْقَرْيَةِ: the home settlement or village from which the traveler departed
key_terms.الْوَقْتُ: the time of prayer, relevant to whether repetition is required
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of prayer, referring here to shortened travel prayer
key_terms.سَفَرٍ: travel or journey that carries legal consequences for prayer
key_terms.صَلَاتُهُ: his prayer, whose validity is being ruled upon
key_terms.نِيَّةِ السَّفَرِ: the intention of travel, which affects the legal status of qasr

ai.seo_question: If a traveler prays qasr and then cannot continue the journey, must the prayer be repeated?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of a traveler who prayed qasr after leaving his town by two farsakhs, but then was unable to continue his journey. The Imam عليه السلام states that the prayer already performed is valid and does not need to be repeated, and the compiler explains possible legal grounds for this ruling based on the remaining prayer time or the persistence of the intention to travel.
